posts.author: ron olson
posts.content_md:
Does anyone have a quick and dirty formula for determining the maximum laser linewidth for displaying (not recording) a transmission H1 with a scene depth of X? I am designing a display system for back-lighting transmssion images with 1-2 meters of scene depth and I am unsure as to how to spec delta lambda. 

LED's with ~20nm bandwidth produce an interesting reconstruction (albeit a bit too abstract) and it got me to wondering if perhaps a laser isn't somewhat overkill.

posts.author: dcgman
posts.content_md:
Since no-one else has had a go at this, I’ll kick off discussions:

According to this site, [http://www.astr.ua.edu/keel/techniques/eye.html](http://www.astr.ua.edu/keel/techniques/eye.html)

the eye’s resolution is 3 arcseconds, which is roughly 1 milliradian (mrad).

The equation representing the fringe spacing (X) recorded in a hologram is 

X=m/Sin(t)........1

m: recording wavelength, t:angle between the reference and object beam.

When recording a transmission hologram of a diffuse object, t varies over a large range. In order to keep things simple, assume that the average or median angle is 45o. Also, assume the recording wavelength is 532nm. Plugging these values into the above equation yields X=752nm.

Rewrite eq 1:

m=XSin(t).........2

differentiate wrt t

dm/dt=XCos(t)..........3

dm=dt XCos(t).......4

We know X=752nm, q=45o, and dt (eye resolution) is 1 mrad. Substituting these into eq. 4 gives

dm= 0.5nm

So your playback laser has to be no broader than 0.5nm

This figure will apply to an ideal thin transmission hologram.

Notice that the depth of the scene doesn’t seem to come into this analysis- which means it probably needs correction!!

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Ron, did you ever try an LED to illuminate the large transmission hologram? If so, how did it turn out?

posts.author: ron olson
posts.content_md: I have tried (and encourage the use of) LED's for lighting abstract transmissions. They are very effective and can be stacked linearly (on a track) to produce red, green and blue images staggered in space. Their bandwidth (~15-20nm) however is a bit wide to maintain "high-definition" playback. Regarding LED's: I have received word from our supplier (OptiLED) that they will be delivering a 3W product (the current standard is 2W) before the end of January.
